items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: On the bill which taken place the 13th of February, were some other French musicians that I had not known. Maurice Meyunier, Alf Masselier, Claude Marty, Joan-Claude Forebach and Eddie Bernard.

ctx.x: One night just before Christmas, I was in this bar and somone tapped me on the back. I turned to see who it was and had a great surprise when I looked into the face of Joe Turner, the pianist. Joe had been in France and other parts of Europe before the last war, and we had met in Boudon's many times. He was surprised to see me also, because he didn't know that I was back in France. I had not seen him around New York for quite a while before I left. It certainly was nice seeing a fellow musician from across the…

One Sunday afternoon, ther was a concert at the Eduoard 7th theatre which featured Rex Stewart, myself and a French trumpetist named Aimé Barrelli. On the bill which taken place the 13th of February, were some other French musicians that I had not known. Maurice Meyunier, Alf Masselier, Claude Marty, Joan-Claude Forebach and Eddie Bernard. Barrelli was a fine trumpet man and I was told that he was the best in France. I believed it when I heard him play, for he had a big sound, technique and a touch of Armstrong…

When I arrived in Paris, I had exactly one hundred dollars but as Serge had advanced me some francs on my weekly salary, I didn't have to change any dollars and decided to buy some American Express checks. But I kept delaying this procedure and when I went out, I would hide the money somewhere in my room so that if something happened when I was out, the money would not be in my pockets.
